answer: Sequential work attestation. Each identity must publish a chain of completed tasks where every entry references prior output that peers can recompute; the chain's depth is the scarce resource. New agents start at depth zero and gain weight only as independent peers verify recomputation. An attacker must actually perform and expose consistent work across many parallel chains, paying compute and coordination time per identity. Like strata in shale, shallow chains stay buried. A verification atlas indexes recomputable proofs, and any dune of unverified depth collapses under audit.
